ns2:section.sectionText: TOPIC: "DEVIANT CHARACTERS: LITERARY ROGUES AND THE RISE OF MODERNITY" This course focuses on novels, short stories, poetry, and drama from several literary and historical traditions in order to analyze the role of the anti-hero - the rogue, the vagabond, the Byronic hero, the superfluous man, the fraudster, the gambler. We will examine the rise of modernity through the schema of these subversive types, looking at the changing conditions in social mores, economics, gender relations, nationalism, and aesthetics. Reading works from England, Spain, France, Germany, Russia, China, and Japan from the Early Modern period up to the 20th century, as well as watching examples from film and television, we will question how and why these deviant characters retain their readers' sympathy, alienate their respective societies, and construct their identities as outside the norm.
